newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto accused some officials of the World Bank of a conspiracy to destabilise her government by depicting a wrong picture of the economy.

- Pakistan will hold crucial talks with the International Monetary Fund from October 1 to 3 on the $600 million Standby Arrangement and on a new $3 billion Extended Structural Adjustment Facility programme.
- Bhutto ruled out dismissal of her government by President Farooq Leghari, saying their relations were normal.
- Pakistan's tea imports fell 21.68 percent to 14,107 tonnes during July-August due to smuggling.
- Sugar prices are likely to remain unstable despite government efforts to import the commodity from India.
- Some eight million tonnes of crude reserves of copper have been identified in North Waziristan.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Unprecedented unloading of shares by financial institutions was being described as the main reason for continuous recession in the stock market.
FINANCIAL POST
- The World Bank said an offshore gas pipeline from Qatar, which could also carry Iranian gas to Pakistan and India, would be exposed to local political events and regional disputes.
THE NEWS
- Afghan government jets bombed the Taleban-held eastern city of Jalalabad killing at least 12 people and wounding 50.

- Food and Agriculture Minister Nawab Yousaf Talpur said a white fly attack in the southern Punjab cotton belt might prevent Pakistan from achieving its cotton target of 10 million 375-lb bales in 1996/97 (July-June).
- The Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan has scrapped an export tender of 30,000 tonnes of basmati rice of 1995/96 crop because it was offered low prices.
THE MUSLIM
- Pakistan has decided to withdraw a 10 percent regulatory duty imposed on imports since October.
- Gold prices have increased on the latest rupee devaluation.
- A Pakistan Air Force fighter crashed near Quetta but the pilot safely baled out.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
